S64.01.needs: AGI Desktop paired with Chrome through the extension, and a signed-in account
S64.01.note: The browser tools are offered to the model only while Chrome is paired (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs, browser_tool_definitions). The /chrome text in the Paired state is in render_chrome_state.
steps: Sign in to AGI Desktop, pair it with Chrome through the extension, and open a web page in Chrome.
In a terminal run agi, then type /chrome and check that it says Chrome integration and Paired. This session can read and act in the browser you are looking at.
At the prompt, ask a question such as: What is the page open in my Chrome about?
Compare the answer with the open page: it should name the page's title and visible content.
For the side-panel route: right-click the page background and choose Ask AGI about this page, then ask a question and check the answer uses the page.
S64.01.where: Terminal: run agi, then type /chrome. Or in Chrome, right-click the page background > Ask AGI about this page (side panel).

labels.text: Send selected text to a local app…

S64.02.needs: a web page with text to select, the AGI Chrome extension, the AGI CLI installed
S64.02.note: A second route exists: right-click the selection and choose Ask AGI about "%s", which opens the side panel with the selection attached (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json). The code line side_panel.ts:16719 is the Copy CLI command handler.
steps: On a web page, highlight some text.
Right-click the highlighted text and choose Send selected text to a local app….
In the preview titled Send selected context?, click Copy CLI command.
Paste into a terminal and run it; the command starts with agi and passes an agi-context:// link to --context-url.
Ask a question about the text at the prompt and check the answer uses the highlighted text and its source page.
S64.02.where: Chrome: select text on a web page > right-click the selection > Send selected text to a local app… > Copy CLI command. Then paste the copied command in a terminal.

S64.06.needs: a Chrome with the AGI extension, a signed-in account
S64.06.note: The CLI route is the same as S64.01: agi, then a free question at the prompt while Chrome is paired.
steps: Open a web page with clear content in Chrome.
Right-click an empty part of the page and choose Ask AGI about this page.
In the AGI side panel, type a free question about the page, such as: What are the main points of this page?
Send it and wait for the answer.
Compare the answer with the page: it should use what the page says, not general knowledge.
S64.06.where: Chrome: right-click the background of a web page > Ask AGI about this page, then type a question in the side panel.

labels.text: The agent wants to open an address in your signed-in Chrome.

S64.10.needs: AGI Desktop paired with Chrome, a signed-in Chrome
S64.10.note: The tool is browser_navigate; there is no separate button for it.
steps: Pair AGI Desktop with Chrome, and run agi in a terminal.
At the prompt type: Open https://example.com in my browser.
When the permission prompt appears reading The agent wants to open an address in your signed-in Chrome., approve it.
Look at the terminal line that starts with Open(https://example.com).
Compare with Chrome: the address should open in a tab in the user's own Chrome.
S64.10.where: Terminal: run agi, then ask the assistant at the prompt to open a web address, for example: Open https://example.com in my browser.

S64.14.needs: AGI Desktop paired with Chrome, a site with a search box
S64.14.note: The search box is found through browser_find, which marks the site's own search field as search (tool_catalog.rs browser_find description). No dedicated search command exists.
steps: Pair Chrome, open a site that has its own search box, and run agi.
At the prompt ask the assistant to search that site for a term.
Approve any permission prompts that appear for Find or Type actions.
Watch the terminal lines such as Find(...) and Read the active tab.
Compare the reply with the site's search results page: it should report the results shown there.
S64.14.where: Terminal: run agi, then ask the assistant at the prompt to search a site, for example: Search the site for pricing and tell me the results.

labels.text: No active tab is open in the paired Chrome, so no fields were filled.

S64.15.needs: AGI Desktop paired with Chrome, a web form open in a signed-in Chrome
S64.15.note: If no tab is open the error No active tab is open in the paired Chrome, so no fields were filled. appears instead, from apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs.
steps: Pair Chrome, open a web form in Chrome, and run agi.
At the prompt ask the assistant to fill in the fields it can see, giving the values.
Approve the permission prompt that lists the tab and fields.
Watch for the terminal line Fill in the form.
Compare the form in Chrome: the fields should hold the values you gave, and the submit button should not have been pressed.
S64.15.where: Terminal: run agi, then ask the assistant at the prompt to fill a form on the open page, for example: Fill in the form on this page with my name and email.

S64.16.needs: AGI Desktop paired with Chrome, a signed-in Chrome
S64.16.note: There is no separate multi-step control; the steps come from the assistant's own tool loop. The code line desktopCommands.ts:202 is the browser_history handler, not the loop.
steps: Pair Chrome with a tab open and run agi.
At the prompt type a goal that needs several website steps.
Approve each permission prompt as it appears.
Watch the terminal lines for each step, such as Open(...), Find(...) and Read the active tab.
Compare the final reply with the goal: it should say what was done across the steps.
S64.16.where: Terminal: run agi, then type a multi-step goal at the prompt, for example: Open https://example.com, find the contact page and read me the email address.

labels.text: The desktop app asks before the first action and records each one in its activity.

S64.18.needs: AGI Desktop paired with Chrome, a signed-in Chrome
S64.18.note: print_tool_status (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/common/mod.rs) prints nothing while the full-screen TUI is active, so confirm the lines show in the TUI transcript too (agent/chat.rs:191).
steps: Pair Chrome with a tab open and run agi.
Ask for a browser task that takes at least two actions, such as: Open https://example.com and click the first link.
Watch the terminal while it runs: each action should appear as its own line, such as Open(...) or Click(...), before the next action starts.
Also check the AGI Desktop activity list, which the /chrome text says records each action.
Compare: every action taken should have a line and nothing should be missing.
S64.18.where: Terminal: run agi, then give a browser task at the prompt; each browser action appears as a terminal line.

S64.32.needs: AGI Desktop paired with Chrome, a signed-in Chrome
S64.32.note: The summary is the assistant's final message; the code (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs) only returns tool results, and no separate summary screen was found.
steps: Pair Chrome and run agi.
Give a browser task that is only partly possible, such as: Open https://example.com and submit the login form.
Wait for the task to end, with the final reply shown in the terminal.
Read the reply: it should say what was done and what still needs the user.
Compare with the Chrome tab: the reply should match what actually happened.
S64.32.where: Terminal: run agi, give a browser task at the prompt, and read the final reply after the task ends.
